name: CKS Runtime, Seccomp & Audit
description: Node-level runtime security you can't practice in CK-X: custom + RuntimeDefault seccomp profiles, read-only root filesystems, API server audit logging, etcd encryption at rest, and ServiceAccount token hardening — all against a real multi-node cluster with node access.
objective: CKS › Runtime Security, Supply-chain & Hardening. Prove you can configure seccomp, API audit logging, and etcd encryption at rest.

questions.title: Custom (Localhost) seccomp profile
questions.prompt:
Confine a workload with a **custom seccomp profile** loaded from the node.

1. On worker node `$W1`, place a seccomp profile JSON at `/var/lib/kubelet/seccomp/profiles/audit.json`. The kubelet's seccomp root is `/var/lib/kubelet/seccomp`, so the profile's *localhost* path is `profiles/audit.json`. A simple auditing profile (default action `SCMP_ACT_LOG`) is fine.
2. Create a pod named `seccomp-audit` in namespace `default` using image `busybox:1.36` running `sleep 3600`, pinned to node `$W1` (via `nodeName` or `nodeSelector`), with a `seccompProfile` of type `Localhost` and `localhostProfile: profiles/audit.json`.

The pod must be **Running**.

_Hint:_ `docker exec -it $W1 bash` to create the profile file; set `spec.securityContext.seccompProfile` (or the container's `securityContext.seccompProfile`).

verification.description: Seccomp profile JSON present at /var/lib/kubelet/seccomp/profiles/audit.json on the worker
Pod seccomp-audit references the Localhost profile profiles/audit.json
Pod seccomp-audit is Running on the worker

questions.title: RuntimeDefault seccomp profile
questions.prompt:
Create a pod named `seccomp-default` in namespace `default` using image `busybox:1.36` running `sleep 3600`, whose `securityContext.seccompProfile.type` is **`RuntimeDefault`** (the container runtime's default profile — the baseline CKS expects on every workload).

The pod must be **Running**.

_Hint:_ set `spec.securityContext.seccompProfile.type: RuntimeDefault`.

verification.description: Pod seccomp-default uses seccompProfile type RuntimeDefault and is Running

questions.title: Read-only root filesystem
questions.prompt:
Create a pod named `readonly-root` in namespace `default` using image `busybox:1.36` running `sleep 3600` with a container `securityContext.readOnlyRootFilesystem: true`.

Because the root FS is read-only, mount an **`emptyDir`** volume at `/tmp` so the process still has a writable scratch area.

The pod must be **Running**.

_Hint:_ set the container `securityContext.readOnlyRootFilesystem: true`, add a `volumes` entry of type `emptyDir`, and `volumeMounts` it at `/tmp`.

verification.description: Pod readonly-root has readOnlyRootFilesystem true with an emptyDir mounted at /tmp

questions.title: API server audit logging
questions.prompt:
Enable **audit logging** on the kube-apiserver running on the control-plane `$CP`.

1. Write an audit policy to `/etc/kubernetes/audit-policy.yaml` on `$CP`. A minimal policy logging everything at `Metadata` level is acceptable.
2. Edit the kube-apiserver static pod manifest (`/etc/kubernetes/manifests/kube-apiserver.yaml`) to add:
   - `--audit-policy-file=/etc/kubernetes/audit-policy.yaml`
   - `--audit-log-path=/var/log/kubernetes/audit.log`
   and the **hostPath volumes + volumeMounts** so both the policy file and the `/var/log/kubernetes` directory are visible inside the apiserver container.

The directory `/var/log/kubernetes` is already created on the node (by lab setup). After the kubelet restarts the apiserver, the audit log file must exist on the node.

_Hint:_ mount the policy file read-only and `/var/log/kubernetes` read-write; the apiserver restarts automatically when you save the manifest. Watch `kubectl -n kube-system get pod kube-apiserver-$CP`. If the apiserver does not come back, you introduced a YAML/flag error — fix the manifest.

verification.description: Audit log file exists at /var/log/kubernetes/audit.log on the control-plane

questions.title: etcd encryption at rest
questions.prompt:
Encrypt Kubernetes **Secrets at rest** in etcd on the control-plane `$CP`.

1. Create an `EncryptionConfiguration` at `/etc/kubernetes/enc/enc.yaml` on `$CP` that encrypts the `secrets` resource using an **`aescbc`** provider (a 32-byte base64 key), with `identity` listed as a fallback. The directory `/etc/kubernetes/enc` is already created by lab setup.
2. Edit the kube-apiserver manifest to add `--encryption-provider-config=/etc/kubernetes/enc/enc.yaml` plus the hostPath volume + mount for `/etc/kubernetes/enc`.
3. After the apiserver restarts, create a Secret named `secret-enc` in namespace `default` (e.g. `kubectl create secret generic secret-enc --from-literal=key=supersecret`).

The Secret, when read directly from etcd, must be stored **encrypted** (its raw value begins with `k8s:enc:aescbc:`), not plaintext.

_Hint:_ generate a key with `head -c 32 /dev/urandom | base64`. If the Secret existed before you enabled encryption you must re-create it (or run `kubectl get secrets -A -o json | kubectl replace -f -`) so it is re-written encrypted.

verification.description: Secret 'secret-enc' is stored encrypted (k8s:enc:aescbc) in etcd

questions.title: ServiceAccount token hardening
questions.prompt:
Stop automatically mounting API tokens into a workload that does not need them.

1. Create a ServiceAccount named `restricted` in namespace `default` with **`automountServiceAccountToken: false`**.
2. Create a pod named `sa-restricted` in namespace `default` using image `busybox:1.36` running `sleep 3600` that uses `serviceAccountName: restricted`.

The pod must be **Running**.

_Hint:_ `automountServiceAccountToken` lives on the ServiceAccount object (and can also be overridden on the pod). Validation checks the SA field and that the pod references the SA.

verification.description: Pod sa-restricted uses the 'restricted' ServiceAccount and is Running
